title: Browser / Playwright MCP — AI Controls a Real Browser

sections.content:
## What You'll Learn

By the end of this lesson you'll have the Playwright MCP installed and working — and you'll have used Claude to open websites, take screenshots, and extract information from real pages.

## What Playwright MCP Does

Playwright is a browser automation framework — it can control Chrome, Firefox, and Safari programmatically. The Playwright MCP server exposes this capability to Claude.

With Playwright MCP, Claude can:
- Navigate to any URL
- Take screenshots of any page
- Click buttons and links
- Fill in forms
- Scroll, hover, and interact with page elements
- Extract text content from pages
- Run JavaScript in the browser context
- Wait for elements to appear before interacting

This is a real browser running on your computer. When Claude navigates to a website using Playwright, a real browser window opens (or runs headlessly in the background). It's not a simulation.

**Real actions on real sites.** Because Playwright controls an actual browser, Claude can interact with real websites — including sites where you're logged in. It can fill forms, click submit buttons, and trigger real actions. Always review what Claude is planning to do before confirming, especially on sites with your account credentials.

## Installation

The Playwright MCP server is maintained by Microsoft. Install it and add it to your config:
Then add it to your global `settings.json`:
**First-run browser download:** The first time Playwright runs, it may need to download browser binaries. This can take a minute or two. If prompted, allow it to complete. This only happens once.

## Practical Use Cases

**Web scraping and monitoring:**
`"Go to news.ycombinator.com and list the top 10 story titles and their URLs."`

**Documentation lookup:**
`"Navigate to docs.anthropic.com and find the page about rate limits. Summarize what it says."`

**Screenshot capture:**
`"Take a screenshot of code.visualstudio.com and describe what's featured on the homepage today."`

**Form filling:**
`"Go to [form URL] and fill in the fields with [values]. Show me the filled form before submitting."`

**Comparison research:**
`"Visit the pricing pages for Vercel, Netlify, and Cloudflare Pages. Compare their free tier limits."`

**Website testing:**
`"Open my about-me.html file in the browser. Check that all links work and take a screenshot of how it looks."`

## Headless vs. Headed Mode

By default, Playwright MCP runs in headed mode — you'll see a browser window open when Claude navigates. This is useful while learning because you can watch exactly what's happening.

For background automation, you can configure it to run headlessly (no visible window):

Add `"--headless"` to the args if you want silent background execution. But for this lesson, keep it headed — watching Claude navigate is the best way to understand what it's doing.

## What Playwright Can't Do

Playwright is not omnipotent:

- **CAPTCHAs** — Most modern CAPTCHA systems detect automation and block it
- **Sites with aggressive bot detection** — Some sites detect Playwright's fingerprint and block it
- **Actions requiring 2FA** — If a site requires two-factor authentication, Playwright can't handle the auth step
- **Flash or legacy plugins** — Modern Playwright doesn't support old plugin technologies

For regular websites, documentation sites, news sites, and public web apps, Playwright works reliably.

sections.title: Web Automation and Information Extraction
sections.content:
**Setup:**
1. Run `npm install -g @playwright/mcp@latest` in PowerShell
2. Add the playwright entry to your `settings.json`
3. Relaunch `claude`, type `/mcp` to confirm `playwright` is listed

**Task 1 — Screenshot and describe:**
Ask: `"Using Playwright, navigate to code.visualstudio.com and take a screenshot. Describe what's on the homepage — what are they currently featuring?"`

Watch the browser window open, navigate, and capture the page.

**Task 2 — Extract live information:**
Ask: `"Go to news.ycombinator.com and list the top 5 story titles, their URLs, and how many points each has."`

**Task 3 — Documentation scraping:**
Ask: `"Navigate to modelcontextprotocol.io and tell me what MCP servers are listed on the homepage or documentation page."`

**Task 4 — Multi-site comparison:**
Ask: `"Visit the free tier pages for both Vercel (vercel.com/pricing) and Netlify (netlify.com/pricing) and compare: bandwidth limits, build minutes, and number of sites allowed on the free tier."`

Watch Claude visit both pages and extract the comparison data.

**Task 5 — Test your own work:**
Ask: `"Use Playwright to open my exercises/about-me.html file in the browser. Take a screenshot, then tell me what it looks like and suggest one visual improvement."`

Note: to open a local file, give the full path: `file:///C:/Users/YourName/Documents/ai-course-projects/exercises/about-me.html`

Save a summary of what Playwright can do to `notes/playwright-capabilities.md`.
**You've completed lesson 8-10.** Claude can now browse the web on your behalf. Lesson 8-11 is the flagship MCP lesson — a real inbox cleanup session with the Gmail MCP.
